headline_marked: Obaidul Quader among [[7 AL leaders sentenced to death]] for July atrocities
headline: Obaidul Quader among 7 AL leaders sentenced to death for July atrocities
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 found the senior leaders guilty of crimes against humanity during the July-August mass uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six other senior party and affiliated organization leaders to death. They were found guilty of crimes against humanity during the July-August mass uprising.

The other convicts include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary Bahauddin Nasim, Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, General Secretary Moinul Hossain Khan Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.

The tribunal ordered the confiscation of 50 percent of the movable and immovable properties of Quader, Arafat, Nasim, Parash, and Nikhil. The proceeds will be used to compensate the victims and the families of those killed during the uprising.

The convicts, who have been absconding throughout the proceedings, were found guilty on multiple charges, including murder and persecution. The verdict follows a seven-month trial involving 29 prosecution witnesses.
Obaidul Quader was sentenced to death on charges of ordering and inciting attacks on protesters, and for his superior command responsibility in failing to prevent mass killings.
Bahauddin Nasim and Mohammad Ali Arafat also received death sentences for their roles in conspiring to suppress the movement and using state machinery to facilitate crimes.

Following the verdict, a crude bomb exploded near the Supreme Court gate. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that CCTV footage identified suspects who could be "AL miscreants," and an investigation is underway.
More than 100 pro-AL lawyers staged a silent protest on the Supreme Court premises, chanting "Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu" in response to the judgment.
caption:
7 top Awami League leaders, including Obaidul Quader, have been sentenced to death for crimes against humanity during the July uprising.

The other convicts include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary Bahauddin Nasim, Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, General Secretary Moinul Hossain Khan Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.

The tribunal ordered the confiscation of 50 percent of the movable and immovable properties of Quader, Arafat, Nasim, Parash, and Nikhil. The proceeds will be used to compensate the victims and the families of those killed during the uprising.

The convicts, who have been absconding throughout the proceedings, were found guilty on multiple charges, including murder and persecution. The verdict follows a seven-month trial involving 29 prosecution witnesses.

Obaidul Quader was sentenced to death on charges of ordering and inciting attacks on protesters, and for his superior command responsibility in failing to prevent mass killings.

Bahauddin Nasim and Mohammad Ali Arafat also received death sentences for their roles in conspiring to suppress the movement and using state machinery to facilitate crimes.

Following the verdict, a crude bomb exploded near the Supreme Court gate. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that CCTV footage identified suspects who could be "AL miscreants," and an investigation is underway.

headline_marked: 7 die, [[1,593 hospitalized for dengue]] in 24 hours
headline: 7 die, 1,593 hospitalized for dengue in 24 hours
summary: Health officials report a surge in cases, with the first 15 days of September showing an alarming increase in both infections and deaths compared to August.
details: Seven people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, while 1,593 new patients were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of those who died, four were women and three were men, with ages ranging from 21 to 75 years. Among the new admissions, 1,004 were men and 589 were women.
Regional data shows that hospitals in the Dhaka division (excluding city corporations) saw the highest number of new admissions with 383 patients, followed by Khulna division with 290.
Since January 1, 2024, a total of 55,163 people have been infected with dengue, and 164 people have died. Of the deceased, 86 are women and 78 are men.
Currently, 4,058 dengue patients remain hospitalized across the country. In the last 24 hours, 1,566 patients were discharged.
Analysis of monthly data reveals a worrying trend: while 20,536 were infected and 43 died in August, 19,317 were infected and 67 died in the first 15 days of September alone.
The Dhaka South City Corporation area has recorded the highest number of deaths, with 51 fatalities reported in hospitals there.
caption:
7 deaths and 1,593 new hospitalizations in just 24 hours. Dengue cases are surging at an alarming rate.

Seven people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, while 1,593 new patients were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

Of those who died, four were women and three were men, with ages ranging from 21 to 75 years. Among the new admissions, 1,004 were men and 589 were women.

Regional data shows that hospitals in the Dhaka division (excluding city corporations) saw the highest number of new admissions with 383 patients, followed by Khulna division with 290.

Since January 1, 2024, a total of 55,163 people have been infected with dengue, and 164 people have died. Of the deceased, 86 are women and 78 are men.

Currently, 4,058 dengue patients remain hospitalized across the country. In the last 24 hours, 1,566 patients were discharged.

Analysis of monthly data reveals a worrying trend: while 20,536 were infected and 43 died in August, 19,317 were infected and 67 died in the first 15 days of September alone.

The Dhaka South City Corporation area has recorded the highest number of deaths, with 51 fatalities reported in hospitals there.
